newsitem.title: CHINA: HK GOLD CLOSES LITTLE CHANGED IN TWO-WAY TRADE.
newsitem.headline: HK GOLD CLOSES LITTLE CHANGED IN TWO-WAY TRADE.

text.p: Hong Kong gold closed little changed on Friday compared to New York's previous close, helped by late short-covering after two-way trading, dealers said.
Bullion ended at US$321.60/322.10 an ounce against New York's US$321.70/322.20 close on Thursday and Hong Kong's previous close of US$318.70/319.20.

"Early profit-taking pushed gold to a day's low of US$321.00/50, but short-covering interest in the afternoon session helped gold to a day's high of US$321.70/322.20," a senior dealer at a local investment house said.
"Unless the metal breaches either side of US$315 or $325, it is likely to be locked in narrow range in the immediate run," another dealer said.
Local gold ended HK$22 higher at HK$2,978 a tael.
The carry over charge at the Chinese Gold and Silver Exchange Society dropped to -6.00 from its previous fix at nil.
